questions.q: What is the first step when creating a new OTBI analysis?
options: Writing a SQL SELECT statement
Selecting a subject area
Scheduling the analysis to run automatically
Publishing to Shared Folders
questions.explain: An analysis begins by choosing the subject area (such as Payables Invoices) that provides the available facts and dimensions.

questions.q: On the Criteria tab, how is an OTBI analysis's query actually defined?
options: By writing a BI Publisher data model
By dragging the facts and dimensions (columns) you want into the selected-columns list
By editing an RTF template
By configuring a duty role
questions.explain: There is no separate query to write — selecting and arranging columns on the Criteria tab is itself the query definition.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the view types available on the Results tab?
options: Table
Pivot Table
Graph
RTF Template
questions.explain: RTF templates belong to BI Publisher's layout design, not to OTBI's Results tab view types (table, pivot table, graph).

questions.q: In the worked example answering "unpaid invoices over $10,000, more than 30 days old," what role does the filter play?
options: It selects the subject area
It restricts the results to rows meeting conditions like Amount > 10,000, Days Overdue > 30, and Status = Unpaid
It schedules the analysis to run nightly
It converts the analysis into a BI Publisher report
questions.explain: Filters narrow the returned rows to those meeting specified conditions, which is how the broad invoice data gets narrowed to the exact request.

questions.q: Where does a finished OTBI analysis get saved by default?
options: It cannot be saved; it must be rebuilt every time
Directly into Shared Folders, visible to everyone immediately
Typically into the user's own My Folders, until published to Shared Folders for others
Into the Scheduled Processes work area
questions.explain: A saved analysis typically lands in the author's My Folders first; publishing to Shared Folders is a separate, deliberate step.
